summary: A portal area: one new API route group (/portal) answering the caller's own month, reserve, holidays and open requests on one side, and a read-time projection over Membership, Vacancy and Project as an organization news feed on the other; a page of its own for every feed entry; and three per-organization group switches an admin owns. A Client draws no entry (REQ-01-032). Nothing writes a feed row — every entry is derived from a source row that already exists, addressed `{kind}:{sourceId}`, computed per read and never stored. One additive migration adds `OrganizationPortalSettings` (absent reads as all three groups enabled, so no backfill). On the web side: a new screen at /org/{orgId}, an entry page at /org/{orgId}/news/{entryId}, a settings screen at /org/{orgId}/settings/portal, a `Team overview` row at the top of the rail, and a move of the post-sign-in destination from the members list to the portal — the one wide edit, 33 `waitForURL('**/members')` waits across 28 e2e files, one of them `signIn` in e2e/tests/helpers.ts. One new test-support fixture, POST /api/test/membership/backdate-joined, because no product route can move a membership's joinedAt and an anniversary needs one. THIS PLAN IS BLOCKED on three spec findings (P1, P2, P3) recorded in pre_implement.verdict.json; the tasks below are what would be executed once those are settled, and the tasks that touch them (T3/T7 the holidays block, T6/T10 the entry counts and the acceptance criterion) name them where they bite.

tasks.title: Shared vocabulary: two capabilities, PORTAL_MESSAGES, the entry-id and cursor codecs, anniversary dates, settings and paging validation
detail: Add `ViewPortalHome` and `ManagePortalSettings` to the `Capability` union in packages/validation/src/roles.ts and to every one of the four `ROLE_CAPABILITIES` rows. `ViewPortalHome` goes in admin, manager, user and viewer; `ManagePortalSettings` in admin alone (Roles & Permission Matrix). The map is `Record<NormalizedRole, readonly Capability[]>` typed against the union, so the compiler forces all four rows to be revisited — do not add a fifth key, and do not add these to `MemberCapability`/`CAPABILITY_MATRIX`: nothing in this spec calls `can(role, ...)` for them.

Every check runs through `normalizeRole()` — `hasCapability(role, 'ViewPortalHome')` already does, so a stored legacy `member` normalizes to `user` and holds it (TC-01-INT-02, TC-01-UNIT-06). A client principal holds no role and must never reach a role-keyed helper (`capabilitiesForPrincipal`, roles.ts:296): the API refusal is OrgScopeGuard's, not this table's.
No route serializes ROLE_CAPABILITIES, so adding two members changes no existing response body — grep for `capabilitiesFor` in apps/api/src returns nothing that answers a caller.

New file packages/validation/src/portal.ts exporting `PORTAL_MESSAGES` with exactly the ten strings from contracts §Error Messages, verbatim: noProject '(No project)', limitInvalid 'Ask for between 1 and 50 entries.', cursorInvalid 'That page marker is not one this feed issued.', groupsInvalid 'Say true or false for People, Hiring and Work.', feedEmptyTitle 'Nothing has happened yet', feedEmptyBody 'When somebody joins, a vacancy opens or a project starts, it shows up here.', monthEmpty 'No time tracked yet this month.', requestsEmpty 'Nothing is waiting on you, and you have asked for nothing.', noCountry 'Nobody has stated your country, so no holiday calendar reaches you.'

`composeEntryId(kind, sourceId, years?)` / `parseEntryId(id)`: `{kind}:{sourceId}`, and `member-anniversary:{membershipId}:{years}` where `{years}` is the anniversary COUNT (contracts' example `member-anniversary:43b4ff02-…:2` sits beside `detail.years: 2`), not a calendar year. The four kinds are `member-joined`, `member-anniversary`, `vacancy-opened`, `project-started` and nothing else — `client-added` is not a kind this release knows (REQ-01-032), and an id naming it parses as an unknown kind, which is a 404 (TC-01-INT-16). `parseEntryId` returns null and never throws for '', 'member-joined', 'nope:abc', 'member-anniversary:abc', 'member-anniversary:abc:zero' (TC-01-UNIT-01).
`composeCursor(instant, entryId)` / `parseCursor(s)`: `{ISO-8601}|{entryId}`, both halves parseable, null on any malformation (contracts §Validation Rules row 2; TC-01-UNIT-02).

`anniversaryDate(joinedAt, years)`: a 29 February joining resolves to 1 March in a non-leap year and to 29 February in a leap one — the first day on or after the nominal date (Edge case 4); the lowest year produced is 1, never 0 (REQ-01-029, TC-01-UNIT-05).

`validatePortalGroups(body)`: all three of `people`, `hiring`, `work` required and strictly boolean — a missing key, a string 'false' and an empty object are each `PORTAL_MESSAGES.groupsInvalid` (TC-01-UNIT-03). `validateFeedLimit(v)`: integer 1–50, `undefined` defaults to 20, `0`/`51`/`'20'` carry `PORTAL_MESSAGES.limitInvalid` (TC-01-UNIT-04).
Export everything added from packages/validation/src/index.ts — the API and the web app both read it from the package root.
allCallSites: apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts#canActivate (the only reader of the Capability union through hasCapability)

concurrency.lock: none — this task writes no row

tasks.title: The migration: OrganizationPortalSettings, one additive table
detail: One model exactly as contracts §Data Model states: `id String @id @default(uuid())`, `organizationId String @unique` FK to Organization with `onDelete: Cascade`, `peopleEnabled`/`hiringEnabled`/`workEnabled` `Boolean @default(true)`, `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt`. Add the back-relation field on `Organization` — the model already carries `holidaySourcing OrganizationHolidaySourcing?`, which is the shape to copy.

No column is added to any existing table, nothing is renamed or dropped, and no existing column becomes NOT NULL. The migration writes no rows: an organization with no row reads all three groups enabled (REQ-01-049), which is why signup is not amended and no backfill exists.
Run `prisma generate` from apps/api, never from the repository root.

migration.note: One new table, no change to any existing one. infra/deploy.sh:27 states that migrations run BEFORE the Terraform rollout of the services, as a one-off task on the new image — new schema first, then the code that uses it. Additive is what makes the reverse safe, which is why a rollback of this release needs no database rollback.

tasks.title: API: the /portal route group and the personal half
detail: A module of its own, registered in app.module.ts. One controller at `@Controller('api/organizations/:orgId')` carrying all five portal routes and delegating to the three services (T3 home, T4 feed/entry, T5 settings). Guard stack per contracts §Routes: `@UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard)` on the class; the three read routes check `hasCapability(role, 'ViewPortalHome')` in the service and throw NotFound when it is false; the settings pair additionally carries `CapabilityGuard` + `@RequireCapability('ManagePortalSettings')`.

Do NOT add `@AllowClientPrincipal()` anywhere in this controller, on any handler, the settings pair included. OrgScopeGuard (apps/api/src/auth/org-scope.guard.ts:37-41) answers a client principal a bare 404 on every :orgId route that does not opt in, and it runs before CapabilityGuard — which is REQ-01-004's whole first two rows and the reason TC-01-INT-01 expects 404 on all five routes.
Every query scopes by `session.organizationId`. The path `orgId` is proven equal by OrgScopeGuard and then never used as a selector (contracts §Security).

REQ-01-010: the month is the calendar month containing the caller's own today, resolved in `Account.timezone` (nullable — schema.prisma) falling back to 'UTC'. Answer `month.today`, `startDate`, `endDate` and `timezone` so TC-01-INT-03 can compare two callers in one organization.

REQ-01-011/012/013/014: sum `TimeEntry.durationMinutes` for `membershipId = caller` and `date` inside the month (`TimeEntry.date` is `@db.Date`, indexed `[membershipId, date]`). `byProject` is one row per project, ordered by minutes descending then project name; a null `projectId` becomes one row with `projectId: null` and `projectName: PORTAL_MESSAGES.noProject`. `daysWithEntry` is the count of distinct `date` values. Do not call ReportsService — that projection is shaped for the report screen and its column contract belongs to another spec.

REQ-01-015/016/053: the reserve block is days only — availableDays, usedDays, pendingDays, totalDaysPerYear — and `timeOff` is `null` in full when the membership has no `MemberFinancials` row. No monetary field is in the DTO type at all: `reserveBalance`, `monthlySalary` and `clientHourlyRate` are not conditionally omitted, they are not part of the contract (TC-01-INT-04 scans the serialised body for all three).

REQ-01-017/018/019: the next three `Holiday` rows on or after the caller's own today, ascending, whose `countryCode` is null or equals the caller's resolved country. Resolve the country with `resolveMemberHolidayCountry(membership.countryCode)` from packages/validation (reports.ts:566) and with nothing else — PATCH-012 removed the organization fallback product-wide and the helper is what the holiday list and Amounts Owed already answer from, so the portal cannot answer a different country than they do. A caller whose resolved country is null is answered the null-country rows alone and `timeOff.countryCode: null` (REQ-01-019). Read `Holiday` directly rather than calling HolidaysService.listHolidays — that route is a calendar-year window, not the next three from today — but reuse its country predicate exactly (holidays.service.ts:111-118).

SEE FINDING P2: the holidays and `countryCode` live inside `timeOff`, which REQ-01-016 makes null in full for a membership with no `MemberFinancials` row — so a member with no financials is answered no holidays and no country, and three cases (TC-01-INT-06, TC-01-INT-07, TC-01-E2E-03) read holidays without stating that financials exist. Do not resolve it by moving `holidays` out of `timeOff`: that is the decision P2 halts the run for.

REQ-01-020/021: at most three `Request` rows with `status = 'open'` where the caller is requester or assignee, ordered overdue first, then `neededBy` ascending nulls last, then `lastActivityAt` descending; `openTotal` is the count under the same filter, before the three are taken. `overdue` is derived per the reading account's timezone and never stored. Answer `id`, `number`, `title`, `counterpartName`, `direction` ('raised' | 'assigned'), `neededBy`, `overdue`, `waitingOnMe` as the contract's body shows. Scope the rows the way requests.service.ts:238-250 scopes `scope=mine` (requester OR assignee, organization-scoped) rather than inventing a second definition; note that its `waitingOnMe` counter spans `['open','answered']` while this panel is `status = 'open'` alone, which is what REQ-01-020 says.

`canManageSettings` on the home body is `hasCapability(role, 'ManagePortalSettings')` — it is what the screen gates the settings control on (REQ-01-052), so the web app never needs a second request to find out.
allCallSites: apps/api/src/portal/portal.controller.ts — the only caller of PortalHomeService

concurrency.lock: none — every route in T3 is a read and REQ-01-054 forbids writing on a read

tasks.title: API: the feed projection, its group switches and field-level withholding, and the entry page
detail: The feed is a read-time projection over three source tables and writes nothing, ever — no row on derivation, no row on read (REQ-01-022, REQ-01-054; TC-01-INT-02 counts rows in every source table before and after ten reads).

Four kinds and their sources: `member-joined` from every `Membership` whose `status` is 'active' at `joinedAt` (a `removed` membership derives nothing, REQ-01-028); `member-anniversary` for every whole year Y >= 1 since an active membership's `joinedAt` whose anniversary date falls in the window; `vacancy-opened` from every `Vacancy` at `createdAt` whatever its `status`; `project-started` from every `Project` at `createdAt` whatever its `status`.

A `Client` derives NOTHING (REQ-01-032) — no query against the Client table appears in this file except the join that reads a project's client NAME for REQ-01-035. Nothing is ever derived from Candidate, Application, ApplicationScheduleEvent, ApplicationCriterion or ApplicationCv (REQ-01-033 — a prohibition, so no join to those tables exists here at all).

Window: source moments in the 365 days ending at the caller's own today, inclusive at both ends — a membership joined exactly 365 days ago is inside (Edge case 3), 364 days is inside and 366 is outside (TC-01-INT-12), and a 366-day membership's first anniversary still falls inside and is drawn.

Order: moment descending, ties broken by entry id ascending. Paging: `cursor` = `{ISO}|{entryId}` (T1's codec) and the answer is the entries strictly after it in that order, at most `limit`, with `nextCursor` present only when more remain. `limit` and `cursor` are re-validated server-side and answer 422 with `PORTAL_MESSAGES.limitInvalid` / `cursorInvalid`.

Groups: people = {member-joined, member-anniversary}, hiring = {vacancy-opened}, work = {project-started}. A group switched off for the organization derives no entry of its kinds (REQ-01-036); the answer says nothing about a group being off (REQ-01-037) — there is no `disabledGroups` key on the body.

Visibility (REQ-01-034's decision table, all sixteen rows): every kind is drawn for every reader. Nothing in the feed is filtered by role in this release — what varies by reader is one FIELD, not an entry. Decide any role question on `normalizeRole(Membership.role)` so a legacy `member` row is judged as `user`.

REQ-01-035/055: `detail.clientName` on a `project-started` entry is the client's name where the reader holds `ViewClients` or is a `ProjectMember` of that project, and is `null` — present, not absent — otherwise, so a project with no client and a project whose client is withheld are indistinguishable in the body (TC-01-INT-15).

The entry route resolves the id, loads the source row, and only then decides visibility — there is no branch that answers before the load, so a malformed id, an unknown kind (`client-added:` among them), a vanished row and a row this caller's feed would not contain are byte-identical 404s (REQ-01-040, REQ-01-041, contracts §Security; TC-01-INT-16 asserts identical bodies). An entry belonging to a group that is switched off is a row this caller's feed would not contain, and is 404 for the same reason.

Entry bodies: `facts` is ordered by the server so the page never decides what to draw first. `vacancy-opened` carries title, `body` = description, categories, interview length and interviewer name, and `shareUrl` = the public booking URL while `Vacancy.status` is 'open', `null` once it is 'closed' (REQ-01-042/043/044; TC-01-INT-17 asserts the two bodies are otherwise identical). `member-joined`/`member-anniversary` carry display name, job title, joinedAt and the active projects the reader may already see them on — for admin/manager every active project the subject is on, for a `user` the intersection with their own ProjectMember rows, for a `viewer` none (apps/api/src/projects/projects.service.ts:154-190 is the shipped shape of 'projects this reader may see') — plus `link` to `/org/{orgId}/members/{id}`, which every staff role may open (REQ-01-045). `project-started` carries the project name, its createdAt, the client under REQ-01-035's condition, and the roster only where the reader holds `manage-projects` or is a `ProjectMember`, omitted entirely otherwise with `link: null` (REQ-01-046/047/056). An archived project keeps its entry and its page draws `Archived` beside the name (Edge case 7).

The entry body carries the same `subject` and `detail` the feed entry carried, alongside `facts`/`body`/`categories`/`shareUrl`/`link`, so REQ-01-039's 'the same sentence the feed drew' is composed once from one pair of fields rather than twice from two different shapes (note N4).

concurrency.lock: none — REQ-01-054 makes both routes pure reads, and an entry has no row to lock

tasks.title: API: the three group switches, and the backdate-joined fixture
detail: GET/PUT `.../portal/settings` both answer `{ groups: { people, hiring, work } }`. Absence of the row reads as all three true (REQ-01-049) and the GET writes nothing to create one.

PUT takes all three booleans — a partial body is 422 `PORTAL_MESSAGES.groupsInvalid`, re-validated server-side through T1's validator — and creates the row in the same transaction as the write when none exists (REQ-01-051). A single-row upsert keyed by the unique `organizationId`; last write wins, which is Edge case 18's decision written down.

The capability refusal is `CapabilityGuard`'s 403 `TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden` (REQ-01-050) — the guard already emits exactly that shape (apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts), so no message is written here. A caller who is not a member of this organization never reaches it: OrgScopeGuard answered them 404 first (REQ-01-004).

POST /api/test/membership/backdate-joined, in the existing test-fixtures controller beside `financials/backdate`: body `{ email, joinedAt }`, sets `Membership.joinedAt` for that account's active membership, `204`. Fenced by the file's own `this.guard(authorization)` wrapper (test-fixtures.controller.ts:33-36), which is the in-memory-mail check plus `assertFixturesOpen` — 404 in production without the token. It reaches no product code path. `Membership.accountId` is `@unique`, so 'the active membership of that account' is a single row.
allCallSites: e2e/tests/helpers.ts — the only caller of the fixture route

concurrency.lock: single-row upsert on the `organizationId` unique index — no `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`. The row is one per organization, edited only by whoever administers it, and Edge case 18 settles the race as last-write-wins: the whole record is replaced, so a lost update is one switch re-flicked and never a half-written row. The fixture's write is a direct update outside the product's paths and takes no lock.

tasks.title: Integration cases for the portal API
detail: TC-01-INT-01..08 in portal.spec.ts (the refusals and the personal half), TC-01-INT-09..12 and 14..18 in portal-feed.spec.ts, TC-01-INT-13 in portal-settings.spec.ts. Each test's name carries its TC id.

TC-01-INT-01 asserts 404 on all five routes for a client contact, the settings pair included, and that no body names the portal. No `@AllowClientPrincipal()` is added to reach a 403 — REQ-01-004's table says the contact never gets one.

Assert status codes, and message text read from `PORTAL_MESSAGES`/`TEMPLATE_MESSAGES` rather than retyped. TC-01-INT-04 scans the serialised home body for 'reserveBalance', 'monthlySalary' and 'clientHourlyRate'; TC-01-INT-14 scans the feed body for the candidate's email and name.

SEE FINDING P3 before writing TC-01-INT-10, TC-01-INT-11 and TC-01-INT-14: each states an entry count that REQ-01-027 makes impossible, because every organization's own memberships — the callers' included — each derive a `member-joined` entry. Do not silently restate the counts and do not switch the People group off to make them hold; the run halts on P3 instead.

Jest here is 29 — the file filter is a positional path. Run `npm test -- test/portal.spec.ts` from apps/api; `--testPathPatterns` is the Jest 30 spelling and this version ignores it silently while running everything.

tasks.title: Web: the home screen at /org/{orgId}
detail: There is no `apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/page.tsx` today — the route REQ-01-001 lands on does not exist and this task creates it. `'use client'`, no server action and no API route; fetch `/api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/...` with `credentials: 'same-origin'` (next.config.mjs rewrites to the API origin).

Two independent questions, two requests, two waits: Q1 (the personal half) and Q2 (the feed) are fetched separately and neither wait holds the other. Q1 failing replaces the three left panels with one `InfoBanner` and leaves the feed standing; Q2 failing shows an `InfoBanner` in the feed column alone. Every request has a failure path and every in-flight flag is cleared in `finally`.

Layout from contracts §Screens: above the `lg` rung a grid of `minmax(0, 1fr)` and a fixed 400px feed column; below it they stack with the personal half first. Each panel is `Card variant='panel'`. Each feed entry is its own panel inside an `<a>` to `/org/{orgId}/news/{entryId}`.

States, exactly as the table lists them: Q1 loading paints the panel headings and the column frame with `Preloader` blocks and never a previous answer; an empty month draws `PORTAL_MESSAGES.monthEmpty` and the timer control and draws NO figures (`portal-month-total` absent, TC-01-E2E-03); a membership with no financials drops `portal-timeoff-panel` in full; no country replaces the holiday list with `PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry` and a link to the profile while the figures stand; no requests draws `PORTAL_MESSAGES.requestsEmpty`; Q2 loading draws three `Preloader` entries as `div`s, not anchors; an empty feed draws `EmptyState` with feedEmptyTitle/feedEmptyBody and the invite control for a caller who may invite; `portal-feed-more` appends and never replaces what is drawn.

SEE FINDING P2: the last two of those states cannot both hold as the cases assert them — the no-country message is drawn inside the Time off panel (mock state 2) and that panel is absent in full when there are no financials. Build the states as §Screens words them and leave the case alone; the run halts on P2.

REQ-01-037: nothing on this screen names a group as switched off. No copy, no tooltip, no empty-state variant distinguishes 'off' from 'nothing happened' (TC-01-E2E-07 asserts no text on the page names Hiring or Work).

REQ-01-052: `portal-feed-settings-link` is drawn only when the home body's `canManageSettings` is true. The feed heading row is `justify-content: space-between` with the heading first, so the heading's left edge does not move when the control is absent (Geometry & motion; TC-01-E2E-06 measures it).

Geometry & motion is normative and each row is a line of this task: `portal-month-total` sits first in a flex band with a fixed `--space-10` gap and `tabular-nums` and grows rightwards into the band's slack; `portal-month-project-row` is a `minmax(0,1fr)` name with ellipsis and nowrap beside an `auto` minutes column; `portal-holiday-row` is a fixed 74px date, a `minmax(0,1fr)` ellipsised name and an `auto` trailing text, never wrapping; `portal-request-row` puts the title FIRST at `minmax(0,1fr)` with the due text and badge `auto` and last, so no row's title starts at a different x; each feed entry is a two-column grid, `auto` mark and `minmax(0,1fr)` body that wraps and grows downwards. No box gets a size its own content decides, and no `min-width`/`min-height` is used to hold one.

The month band draws TWO figures — tracked minutes and days with an entry — because those are the only two the contract answers; the mock's third ('Yesterday 5h 22m') and its per-project percentage bar have no field behind them (note N1).

The day separator ('Today', 'Earlier this week') is a block in the column's flow with its own top padding — it never overlays an entry, and nothing on this screen is drawn outside its own flow, so no ancestor's overflow gains a box it does not contain. The one absolutely-positioned box any of these controls opens is a `Select` list, which the design system portals.

`entry-sentence.tsx` composes an entry's sentence from `kind` + `subject` + `detail` and is the ONE place it is written, used by the feed and by the entry page (T8), so REQ-01-039's 'the same sentence' has one source. The strings are the mock's, verbatim, for the four kinds that exist: '{name} joined the team as a {jobTitle}.', 'A vacancy is open: {title}.', '{project} started for {client}.' — and '{project} started.' where `clientName` is null (mock state 8) — '{name} has been with the team for {years} years.'
No hardcoded colour or size: tokens only (`var(--space-3)`, `var(--font-size-s)`, `var(--text-secondary)`), imports from `@devscribed/ds` at the package root only.

Every testid from contracts §Required data-testid: portal-greeting, portal-month-total, portal-month-days, portal-month-project-row, portal-month-empty, portal-timeoff-available, portal-timeoff-panel, portal-holiday-row, portal-holidays-no-country, portal-request-row, portal-requests-empty, portal-feed-entry, portal-feed-empty, portal-feed-more, portal-feed-settings-link.

tasks.title: Web: the entry page and the portal settings screen
detail: The entry page is headed by the sentence T7's `entry-sentence.tsx` composes, from the same `subject`/`detail` pair the feed carried (REQ-01-039). Under it: the timestamp, the server-ordered `facts` as a definition list, `categories` as `Badge` `neutral`, `body` as prose on a vacancy entry only, and `portal-entry-share` while `shareUrl` is non-null. `portal-entry-back` is painted immediately, before any answer, because it needs none. A 404 from the route renders the app's own not-found screen — there is no 'this entry is not for you' state (REQ-01-040).

Geometry: the reading column is capped at 720px and the title wraps inside it; the share URL is a `flex: 1; min-width: 0` code box with ellipsis beside an `auto` copy button, so a long slug never pushes the button off the panel. The copy control follows the shipped one at apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/hiring/vacancies/page.tsx — a refused clipboard says so rather than failing silently.

The settings screen draws the three group switches (`Switch` from @devscribed/ds) with the mock's labels and descriptions and a save button. The submit button is never disabled for validation: the screen owns three booleans and always has a valid body. Testids: portal-settings-group-people, portal-settings-group-hiring, portal-settings-group-work, portal-settings-save; plus portal-entry-title, portal-entry-back, portal-entry-body, portal-entry-share, portal-entry-fact on the entry page.

The mock's settings state draws no save control while contracts §Required data-testid and TC-01-E2E-09 both require `portal-settings-save`; build the save button — the contract and the case agree and the mock is the odd one out (note N5).

tasks.title: E2E cases, and the two measurements they need
detail: TC-01-E2E-01..09 in one file, each test named with its TC id. Selectors are `data-testid` only, from contracts §Required data-testid — the repository's single exception is a navigation control reached by its accessible name, and `nav-portal` is given a testid by the contract, so it is asserted by id.

notes.note: The mock's month panel draws three figures (tracked, days with an entry, and 'Yesterday 5h 22m'), a percentage bar per project, and a project row labelled 'Aurora — Northwind Ltd'. The contract answers `totalMinutes`, `daysWithEntry` and `byProject` rows of `{projectId, projectName, minutes}` — no yesterday figure and no client name — and REQ-01-011/012/014 ask for nothing more. The Geometry & motion row for `portal-month-total` says 'the two figures beside it', which counts the mock's three. The testid table names two and only two. Built to the contract: two figures, project name only.

TC-01-E2E-08 says it 'uses the probes in e2e/tests/ui-invariants.ts'. That file exports five — expectHoldsBox, expectNoScrollGrowth, expectSurvivesReread, expectMessageOnce, expectMessageAbsent — and none measures a shared left edge across rows or a shared right edge across cells. T10 adds the two, in that file, rather than inlining the arithmetic in the spec file.

Five further paths still send a person to the members list and no requirement speaks about any of them: signup (SignupForm.tsx:101), invitation acceptance, the rail's wordmark, and the unauthorized-visitor redirects in clients, clients/[clientId], settings/holidays and settings/request-topics. They are left alone — contracts §Screens names the login form as the one undrawn screen this spec changes. A person may want the wordmark and the signup landing to move too, but that is a decision, not a consequence.

The entry contract's example body carries `subject`, `facts`, `categories`, `body`, `shareUrl` and `link` — and no `detail`. REQ-01-039 requires the page to be headed by the same sentence the feed drew, and that sentence is composed from `detail.jobTitle`, `detail.years` and `detail.clientName`. Composing it from `facts` instead would be a second, differently-shaped source for one string. T4 answers `detail` on the entry body too; it is additive and contradicts nothing the contract states.

The mock's settings state draws three switches and no save control, while contracts §Required data-testid requires `portal-settings-save` and TC-01-E2E-09 presses it. Contract and case agree; the mock is the odd one out. Built with a save button.

The settings screen is the mock's fifth state and has a route, four testids and an E2E case, but `## Screens` §States lists only Q1, Q2 and Q3 and `## Geometry & motion` has no row for it. Its content is fixed copy and three switches, so no box on it is sized by data — which is why this is a note and not a finding. T8 builds it from the mock.

Contracts §Routes cites REQ-01-015 for 'No monetary field appears anywhere in this body'. REQ-01-015 is 'the reserve is answered in days'; the no-money rule is REQ-01-053. A mis-citation, not a disagreement — both requirements point the same way.

TC-01-INT-12 says a membership backdated 366 days has its first anniversary 'two days ago'. joinedAt + 1 year from 366 days ago falls one day ago, or today across a leap day. The arithmetic is off by one; the assertion — that the anniversary is inside the window and drawn — is unaffected. Write the case against the window, not against the literal 'two days'.

REQ-01-021 answers `requests.openTotal` 'so the screen can say how many are not in the three', and nothing draws it: the mock's requests panel has three rows and an 'All requests →' link, there is no message for it in the Error Messages table and no testid. The field is answered and asserted at integration (TC-01-INT-08); the screen draws the link the mock draws.

The feed's own copy — 'joined the team as a', 'A vacancy is open:', 'started for', 'has been with the team for N years' — exists only in the mock. It is product text, not validation text, and T7 puts it in one composer rather than inline in two components. The strings are taken verbatim from the mock; none is invented.

Stale sentences the client-entry removal left behind, in documents this plan reads: §Roles & Permission Matrix says 'what varies is which entries the answer contains, and that is REQ-01-040's table' — REQ-01-040 is the entry-page 404 rule, the visibility table is REQ-01-034, and since REQ-01-032 dropped the client kind that table varies by nothing; specs/portal/README.md §Product decisions still lists the projection as being over 'Membership, Vacancy, Project and Client' and still carries a row 'Client entries | Withheld from user and viewer'; TC-01-INT-10 says a project-started's clientName difference is 'covered by TC-01-INT-11', which covers ordering and paging — TC-01-INT-15 is the case that covers it. None of these changes what is built: REQ-01-032, REQ-01-034 and REQ-01-035/055 are unambiguous. Finding P1 is the one place a stale sentence is not recoverable.

REQ-01-020 says 'open requests'. `Request.status` has a literal value 'open' beside 'answered', and the requests area's own waiting-on-me counter spans both. The portal panel is `status = 'open'` alone — the spec names the status the schema names, and TC-01-INT-08 seeds five rows in that state and expects openTotal 5. An 'answered' request is not drawn.

Acceptance Criterion 2 ('A client contact signing in still arrives at their requests page') names TC-01-INT-01 as its observer, and that case calls five routes as a contact and never observes a landing. No case in the bundle observes REQ-01-002. The behaviour is unchanged code (LoginForm's client branch is untouched), so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect — recorded so nobody reads criterion 2 as verified.
